transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this... it's probably nothing major, just a little embarrassing to admit. 

I came in because, well, my mind just keeps going blank at the worst times. I work as a flagger, and lately I'll just look at the road-closure forms, or even just be holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. Things I've done for years, you know? 

I'm sure it's just me being a little scattered, or maybe I'm just not focusing hard enough, but it's making me worry about doing a good job at work. Is that... I mean, does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
When your mind goes blank, do you ever feel like you're detached from yourself or that things around you don't seem real?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't think so? I always know who I am and where I am, I promise. It's just... it's just a little brain fog, I think. Like when you walk into a room and forget why you went in there, but maybe just a tiny bit worse? 

I definitely don't feel detached or anything weird like that. I'm still me, and everything around me is totally normal. I just... I just get a little confused sometimes. That's pretty common, right? I'm sure it's just stress or something silly. I really hope I'm not making a big deal out of nothing.
Have you noticed any memory problems or difficulty thinking clearly in other parts of your life, like at home or with friends, or is this mostly happening while you're at work?

Um, well... like I mentioned a minute ago, it really just hits me the hardest at work. That's why I brought up the road-closure forms and the stop-slow paddle. It's just so embarrassing to be standing there and suddenly not remember the steps for something I've done for years, so that's what worries me the most. 

At home or with friends... I mean, maybe my mind goes blank a little bit there too? But nothing major, I promise. Just normal stuff, like losing my train of thought mid-sentence or forgetting what I was about to say. I think everyone does that sometimes, right? So it's mostly just at work where it feels... noticeable. I hope I'm answering your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're not at work, do you ever find yourself struggling to remember simple things or concentrate on tasks, like watching TV, reading, or following a conversation?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? Like, sometimes if I'm trying to watch a show or read a book, I might have to go back and re-read a page, or rewind a scene because I just sort of... zoned out. But I really think that's just because I'm tired, you know? 

But honestly, the main thing, the thing that really made me want to come see you, is just what I was saying before. It's just that my mind keeps going completely blank at the worst times. Like I said, I'll be looking right at the road-closure forms, or holding my stop-slow paddle, and I just suddenly cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years! 

I just want to be a good employee and do my job right, so that's what's really bothering me. The home stuff is probably just normal tiredness, right? I'm sorry if I'm repeating myself, I just want to make sure I'm explaining the important part clearly. Am I making sense?
When you're at home, do you ever have trouble remembering things or staying focused even when you're not tired?

Um, well... I mean, I guess it's possible? But honestly, I really try to just push through it when I'm at home. I don't want to make a fuss over every little thing. I'm sure it's just normal stress or getting older, right? 

But really, the main reason I'm here, the thing that's actually a problem, is what I mentioned before. It's just so embarrassing... I came in because my mind keeps going blank at the absolute worst times. Like I said, I'll look right at the road-closure forms, or I'll be holding the stop-slow paddle, and I just suddenly cannot remember the steps. And I've done this job for years! That's not normal, is it? I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job at work, so that's what I'm really worried about. I hope it's okay that I keep bringing that up, I just want to make sure you understand how much it's bothering me. Am I explaining it right?
Can you think of a time when you were well-rested and not stressed, where you still had trouble remembering things or staying focused?

Oh, um... I'm trying to think. I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm not giving you the answers you're looking for. I guess I just don't notice it as much at home, even if I am fully rested. 

But... I know I keep saying this, and I really don't mean to sound like a broken record... but even on days where I slept perfectly fine and don't feel stressed at all, it still happens to me on the job. That's really the whole reason I made this appointment. I'll just be standing out there, holding the stop-slow paddle or looking down at the closure forms, and my brain just completely empties out. All the steps I've taken a thousand times just vanish. 

I'm so sorry to keep bringing it back to work, I just... I really want to be helpful and give you the right information, and that's just where it's the most terrifying for me. Is it okay that I keep focusing on that? I hope I'm not frustrating you.
When your mind goes blank, do you also have trouble paying attention, making decisions, or finding the right words when you're speaking?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit with the words? Like, sometimes I might pause to find the right one, but I think everyone does that, right? I try really hard to pay attention and make good decisions, especially when I'm out there on the road. I don't want you to think I'm completely losing my mind or anything... I'm really trying my best to keep it together.

But, um... yeah, it's mostly just that blankness I keep talking about. I'm sorry, I know I've said it like three times already. It's just... I'll be looking right at the forms, or holding my paddle, and the steps just disappear from my head. It's so embarrassing because I've done it for so long, and I should know better. I just want to be a good worker. I hope I'm answering your question okay... I'm not trying to be difficult, I promise. Does that make sense?
Can you tell me more about how often this happens at work and how much it affects your ability to complete your tasks as a flagger?

Um, well... I mean, I guess it happens enough that people started to notice. I really, really tried to hide it and just work harder, you know? But... well, I guess I stopped being as reliable as I used to be. It's so hard to admit that. I just couldn't finish the road-closure paperwork properly, and... and I stopped trusting myself with the traffic-safety steps. I didn't want anyone to get hurt because of me, so I guess I kind of pulled back. 

And, um, it wasn't just work, either. I feel awful about this, but I started pulling away from everything. I stopped going to choir, I stopped volunteering... I even kind of shut out my family. I just didn't want them to see me struggling and be disappointed in me. I tried so hard to act like everything was fine, but they finally felt like they had to bring me in to get help. I'm really sorry if that makes me sound like a terrible employee or a bad person. I just got so overwhelmed. Do you think I did the right thing by stepping back when I couldn't trust myself? I hope you don't think less of me for letting things get this bad.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, even when you're not at work?

Um... well... I guess I have been feeling a little down lately. I mean, I know everyone gets sad sometimes, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or throwing a pity party for myself. I know I have a lot to be thankful for. 

But... yeah, I guess it's been pretty hard. Most mornings, I just... I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness right in my chest. It's like... like the whole day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. I try to push past it, I really do, because I want to be productive and cheerful for everyone else. But it's just so heavy. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds so dramatic. I'm probably just letting things get to me too much, right? I really am trying to keep a positive attitude. I hope you don't think I'm just giving up or being lazy... is it normal to feel that way sometimes?
Have you been feeling tired or lacking energy most days, even when you get enough rest?

Um... no, I don't think so. I really try to make sure I get enough sleep so I can be ready for the day. I don't want to be one of those people who just lies around, you know? I always try to push myself to keep my energy up, especially because being a flagger means I have to be on my feet and alert. 

So, um, I think my energy levels are mostly okay. I mean, I get a little tired after a long shift, but I think everyone does, right? I'm not just sitting around being lazy, I promise. I really try to pull my weight. I hope that answers your question okay... did I explain that right?
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you used to really like, like choir or volunteering?

Um... well... I guess I have noticed a change, maybe. I mean, I used to be so involved, you know? I was the one organizing all the rides for choir, setting up neighborhood garden swaps, and even coordinating the snacks for the youth basketball games. I always wanted to be helpful and make sure everyone was taken care of. 

But lately... um, I don't know, it's embarrassing to admit. I just... I don't feel that same drive anymore. I can sit on my couch for hours, just staring at my phone, and I see the messages coming in, but I just... I don't feel any push to answer anybody. I feel terrible about it, really I do. I know people are counting on me, and I hate letting them down. I'm not trying to be selfish or ignore my friends, I promise. It's just... it's like the spark for doing those things is just gone right now. 

I hope you don't think I'm just being a bad friend or turning into a recluse. I really do want to be that helpful person again. Is it... is it okay that I'm struggling with this right now? I'm trying to get better, I really am.
Outside of work, do you find it hard to think clearly, make decisions, or focus on things you're trying to do, even when you're not tired?

Um... well... I guess that's actually kind of why I came in to see you. I really don't want to sound incompetent, because I take my job very seriously and I always try to do my best, but... 

Lately, my mind just... it keeps going blank. And it happens at the worst times. Like, I'll be looking at the road-closure forms, or even just holding my stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I just... I cannot remember the steps. And these are things I've done for years! I feel so silly even saying it out loud. 

I try really hard to cover it up so nobody notices, because I don't want anyone to think I can't handle my responsibilities. I'm not losing my mind, am I? I'm really trying to stay focused, but it's just like my brain hits a wall. I hope that makes sense... is it normal to get a little forgetful like that when you're feeling down?
Would you say that most days, your mood feels more down than not, even when there's nothing particularly wrong happening?

Um... well... I guess I do feel a little down sometimes. I mean, I try really hard to stay positive, you know? I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down with me. I always try to put on a smile for the construction crew and the drivers. 

But... um, if I'm being completely honest—and I hope this doesn't make me sound ungrateful for my life or anything—most mornings, I just... I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness right here in my chest. It's like... like the day is already ruined before I even put my feet on the floor. I really try to shake it off, I promise. I know I shouldn't feel that way when there's nothing actually wrong. It's just... hard to push past it sometimes. 

Does that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude, I really am.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you used to really like, like choir or volunteering?

Oh, um... I think I might have mentioned that just a little bit earlier? I hope it was okay that I brought it up before, I really didn't mean to talk out of turn or jump ahead... 

But yes, it's... it's exactly like I was saying. I used to be the one organizing all the choir rides, and putting together the neighborhood garden swaps, and making sure we had the snacks for the youth basketball games. I really loved doing it, and I always want to be someone people can rely on. 

But lately, I just... I can sit for hours just staring at my phone. People will message me, and I just don't feel that push to answer anybody anymore. I feel so incredibly guilty about it, I really do. I promise I'm not trying to be a bad friend or avoid people on purpose, it's just like the energy for it is completely gone. I really want to get back to being helpful again. Is it... is it normal to lose your drive like that when you're going through a tough time? I'm really trying my best to snap out of it.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, even activities you used to really like, like choir or volunteering?

Um... I think we might have just touched on that, actually? I hope it's okay that I brought it up a second ago, I really don't mean to be repeating myself or wasting your time...

But yes, it's... it's just like I was saying. I used to be the one organizing all the choir rides, and setting up the neighborhood garden swaps, and making sure we had snacks for the youth basketball games. I really loved being that person, you know? I always want to be someone people can count on.

But lately... I just... I can sit for hours just staring at my phone. People will message me, and I just don't feel that push to answer anybody anymore. I feel so awful about it, I really do. I promise I'm not trying to be a bad friend or avoid people on purpose, it's just like the energy for it is completely gone. I really want to get back to being helpful again. Is it... is it normal to lose your drive like that when you're going through a tough time? I'm really trying my best to snap out of it, I promise.
Have you completely stopped enjoying activities that used to bring you joy, like choir or volunteering, or do you still get some pleasure out of them even if you’re not as involved?

Oh, goodness, I'm so sorry... I must not have answered you clearly just a moment ago. I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or talk in circles. 

To answer your question about the joy... um... I think... I think the joy is just completely gone. It's not just that I'm less involved. Like I was saying about the garden swaps and the choir rides and the snacks... I used to get so much genuine happiness from doing all of that. It made me feel so good to be there for everyone. 

But now, when I'm just sitting there for hours staring at my phone... even if I think about going, or if I read a message from the choir director, I don't feel that spark of pleasure at all. I don't feel anything good. I just feel... blank. And then I feel terrible because I can't even find the push to just type a reply back to them. I don't get any pleasure out of it right now, even from a distance. 

Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I really hope I'm not sounding too pessimistic. I don't want you to think I've just given up, because I really do want to enjoy those things again.
